post.summary: Get permission to upload a file
post.description:
**Who can use this:** signed-in vendor owners or riders or customers.

Returns a signed form for **direct upload to Cloudinary** (the file never passes through our server). Each kind of upload belongs to one account type:

| `kind` | For | Stored |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor-docs` | vendor owners (CNIC, shop photos) | privately, never a public URL |
| `rider-photo` | riders (profile photo customers see) | publicly |
| `delivery-proof` | riders (proof-of-delivery photo) | privately |
| `complaint` | customers (photos for a complaint) | privately |

1. Call this endpoint.
2. Upload each file to `https://api.cloudinary.com/v1_1/{cloud_name}/image/upload` as `multipart/form-data` with the returned fields (`api_key`, `timestamp`, `signature`, `folder`, `upload_preset`, `type`) plus `file`.
3. Send the returned `public_id` values to `POST /vendor/register` (vendors), `POST /rider/register` (rider photo), `POST /rider/jobs/{id}/complete` (delivery proof) or `POST /orders/{orderId}/complaints` (complaint photos).

Allowed: JPG, PNG or WebP up to 5 MB (checked again on the server). 30 signatures per hour.

get.description:
**Who can use this:** signed-in customers or vendor owners or vendor staff or admins.

A `text/event-stream` that pushes every status change as it happens. **Swagger UI cannot display a live stream** — use a real client:

```js
import { fetchEventSource } from '@microsoft/fetch-event-source';
fetchEventSource(`/api/v1/orders/${id}/events`, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}` },
  onmessage(e) { if (e.event === "status") show(JSON.parse(e.data)); },
});
```

- Each `status` event has an `id`. After a dropped connection, reconnect with the `Last-Event-ID` header to receive what you missed.
- A fresh connection starts with the current status.
- A `ping` event arrives every 25 seconds to keep the connection open.
- The native `EventSource` cannot send an Authorization header; use a fetch-based client.
- If you cannot keep a stream open, poll `GET /orders/{id}` every 15–30 seconds.

info.title: Dhoblio API
info.description:
Laundry & dry-cleaning marketplace for Pakistan. Customers order, vendors work the orders, admins run the platform.

## Try it in 30 seconds

1. Open **Auth → Send a login code** → *Try it out* → *Execute*. In development no SMS is sent.
2. Open **Auth → Sign in with the code** → *Try it out* → *Execute* (the code is always `123456`).
3. That's it: **the access token is applied automatically** (look at the padlock on the *Authorize* button).
   Every endpoint with a padlock now works as that user. Tokens last 15 minutes; call *Get a new access token* to renew.

| To try… | Sign in as |
|---|---|
| Ordering (customer) | any new phone, e.g. `03001234567` |
| The vendor panel | `03000000011` (Lahore), `03000000012` (Karachi), `03000000013` (Islamabad) |
| Vendor review (pending shop) | `03000000019` |
| The rider app | any new phone, choosing role `RIDER` when you sign in, then *Apply to ride* (an admin approves it) |
| Admin | *Admin sign-in* with `admin@dhoblio.local` / `ChangeMe!12345` |

A full customer journey: **Find vendors near me** → **Vendor price list** → **Available pickup / delivery windows** → **Price estimate** → **Place an order**.
Then switch to the vendor account to **Accept** it and move it along.

## How responses look

- Success: `{ "data": … }`, and lists add `"meta": { "nextCursor": "…" }` (pass it as `?cursor=`; `null` = last page).
- Failure: `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details?", "requestId" } }`. Branch on **`code`**, not `message`. Each endpoint below lists the codes it can return.
- **Money** is a string with two decimals in PKR (`"1250.00"`), never a float.
- **Times** are ISO 8601 in UTC (`2026-10-24T05:00:00.000Z`); the business day is Pakistan time (UTC+5).
- Sign-in uses a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.
- Rate limits answer `429` with `details.retryAfterSec`.
- Request/response field details are in **Schemas** at the bottom; each field has a description and example.

## Who can do what

| Role | Can |
|---|---|
| Customer | browse, build a cart, place and track orders, manage addresses |
| Vendor owner | register the shop, set hours and prices, work orders, manage staff |
| Vendor staff | work orders and switch Open / Busy / Closed |
| Rider | apply, go online, take pickup and delivery jobs, prove delivery, see earnings |
| Admin | review vendors and riders, run the dispatch board, support orders, set city fees and couriers |
